Credited to Anna Magdalena Bach, who did not write it. The H number is the Helm catalogue of her stepson, and IMSLP files the set as '4 Pieces for Anna Magdalena Bach, H.1 (Bach, Carl Philipp Emanuel)'. Her name is in the title because the pieces were written FOR her notebook.

Credited to 'Anna Magdalena Bach Notebook', which is the manuscript the piece was copied into rather than anybody who wrote it. BWV Anh. is the appendix of works NOT by Johann Sebastian, and IMSLP catalogues this march under Carl Philipp Emanuel. Commercial editions still print his father's name; the Anhang number is the argument against it.

The credit ran three things together - a name, a BWV number and the notebook. IMSLP and Bach Digital both file BWV 515 under Johann Sebastian. Authorship is genuinely divided: New Grove assigns the melody tentatively to Gottfried Heinrich Bach and the bass certainly to Johann Sebastian, so his is the defensible single name.

The score carries no creator at all - only an engraved title line reading 'Ave Maria - Cherubini', which the import took for the composer. The title was welded onto the surname, so the piece opened a person page called 'Ave Maria Cherubini' and the real composer had none. Luigi Cherubini (1760-1842) is the only Cherubini in the repertoire and set the Ave Maria more than once.

title: The Art of Finger Dexterity, Op. 740 No. 1: Action of the Fingers, the Hand Quiet
why: Seven studies of Op. 740 were all titled with the name of the whole book, and the book's own title misspelled "of" as "Oof". Each score prints its number and the technique it trains above the first system, which is what Czerny called it and what tells one study from the six beside it.
